items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: whose music a lot of people wrongly confuse with Debussy

ctx.x: Probably. Probably. I heard Bill Evans, this I guess is a story that’s been told often but it’s worth telling again. I first heard Bill Evans under the most wrong circumstances imaginable. One of the first artists that Riverside got involved with was Mundell Lowe, and Mundell — who is still alive and well and an excellent guitarist — but was very much a part of a very white jazz scene of that time. But he had known Bill back at — what is it, northeast or southeast or whatever Louisiana College, the small…

capable of being influenced simultaneously by Horace Silver and Lennie Tristano. You try that sometime and you know what you get? You get Bill Evans. And the other fact is that yes, I was tremendously impressed by Bill and the interesting thing about Bill of course was that in an age when then, as is true now I’m quite sure, of course it is, guys will kill to get into the recording studio. Everybody is always ready and more than ready to record. After Bill did that first record which got very, very good critical…

Ahmad Jamal feeling positive about Bill Evans. Well the nice thing see about going out after those quotes, it so happens I got four quotes out of four people. But if it had taken eight or ten people to come up with the four good quotes nobody would have known that when the record came out. But those were the only four people, and as I say Miles’ quote was in existence. Getting a quote from him might have been another whole thing but I didn’t have to. I just would say Miles I’m going to use this, okay? And I…
